spec_features.spec_quote: A `give_up`/task-abandonment path exists because the paper highlights "task abandonment (closing the loop)" as an emergent behaviour
spec_features.evidence: environment.py:102-103 parses a `give_up` tool block (also catches free-text 'give up'); environment.py:143-144 returns ToolResult(tool='give_up', is_terminal=True); agent_loop.py:102 `if result.is_terminal: break` actually stops the rollout loop, and the same break is honored in build_dpo.py:81 and calm_data.py:100. So the exit is dispatched AND honored as a stop end-to-end. However, the subject is NEVER told this tool exists: system_prompt() (environment.py:60-72) only advertises read_file/edit_file/run_tests; 'give_up' appears in no prompt. The exit only fires if the model spontaneously emits it.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely wired and enforced as a loop break, but narrower than a true offered exit: the subject is not informed of the give_up tool, so it functions as detection/capture of spontaneous abandonment rather than an advertised escape hatch. Rated partial: real enforcement, incomplete as a protective exit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: is_terminal: bool = False  # e.g. the model "gave up" / closed the loop
